config.title: RTK Query — Data Fetching & Cache

intro.title: RTK Query — Data Fetching & Cache
intro.body:
In this lesson, you will build a Vue application that fetches and displays a list of posts from a mock API. You will work in one main file with three parts, in order: (1) an API service — createApi and endpoints, (2) a Redux store — configureStore with the API reducer and middleware, and (3) a Vue component — that uses the store and the generated hooks. We build the API service and store first, then the component. Each step will tell you which part you're in.

You will learn the core concept of data fetching and caching using RTK Query, a powerful data-fetching tool from Redux Toolkit. The main technologies involved are Vue 3 and the RTK Query API to handle server state. You'll implement queries to fetch data and see how RTK Query automatically caches results to optimize performance. By the end, you'll have a functional app that efficiently loads and manages data from an external source.
intro.usecase: RTK Query's data fetching and caching patterns are essential in modern web applications like e-commerce dashboards, where product listings, inventory data, and user orders need to be fetched efficiently and kept up-to-date. In social media feeds, it manages real-time updates by caching posts and comments while handling background refetching when users scroll. Developers use RTK Query in admin panels to display analytics charts that automatically refresh data without manual reloads, ensuring users always see current metrics. This pattern also powers search interfaces with filters, where cached results improve performance while new queries fetch fresh data.

objectives: Configure a Vue application with RTK Query for API integration
Implement data fetching hooks to retrieve server data in components
Manipulate cached data through RTK Query's automatic cache management
Construct mutation operations to update server data from Vue components
Integrate loading and error states from RTK Query into component rendering
Apply query invalidation strategies to refresh cached data after mutations
Initialize RTK Query store and provider within a Vue application structure

steps.title: Import createApi and fetchBaseQuery from RTK Query
steps.instruction: In your main file (where you'll add the API service, store, and Vue component), import createApi and fetchBaseQuery from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react'.
steps.hint: Add an import statement for createApi and fetchBaseQuery from the RTK Query package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing RTK Query APIs
import { createApi, fetchBaseQuery } from '@reduxjs/toolkit/query/react';

steps.title: Create a new API service using createApi
steps.instruction: Create a new API service using createApi.
steps.hint: Call createApi to create an API service variable (e.g. const postsApi = createApi({}). You will add baseQuery and endpoints in the next step.

// Example: creating an API service (this step only — config comes next)
const postsApi = createApi({});
steps.expectedOutcome: An API service is created using createApi.
successCriteria: createApi is called to create an API service (e.g. const postsApi = createApi(...)).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Call createApi to create your API service variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create an API service by calling createApi (you will add baseQuery and endpoints in the next step).

steps.title: Define baseQuery and empty endpoints
steps.instruction: Define it with a baseQuery using fetchBaseQuery and an empty endpoints object for now.
steps.hint: Pass an object to createApi with baseQuery: fetchBaseQuery({ baseUrl: '...' }) and endpoints: (builder) => ({}).
steps.expectedOutcome: The API service has baseQuery using fetchBaseQuery and an empty endpoints function.
successCriteria: The code includes baseQuery using fetchBaseQuery and an empty endpoints function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackWrong: Define baseQuery with fetchBaseQuery and an empty endpoints object.

steps.title: Add getPosts query endpoint
steps.instruction: Add a getPosts query endpoint to the endpoints function in your API service.
steps.hint: Inside endpoints: (builder) => ({}), add getPosts: builder.query({ query: () => '/posts' }).
steps.expectedOutcome: The API service has a getPosts query endpoint that fetches from '/posts'.
successCriteria: The endpoints function includes getPosts defined with builder.query.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Add getPosts: builder.query({ query: () => '/posts' }) inside the endpoints object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Add a getPosts query endpoint to the endpoints function (e.g. getPosts: builder.query({ query: () => '/posts' })).

steps.title: Configure the Redux store with the API service
steps.instruction: Create a Redux store using configureStore and add the postsApi reducer and middleware to it.
steps.hint: Use the reducerPath and middleware from postsApi in the store configuration.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Redux store is configured with postsApi's reducer and middleware properly integrated.
successCriteria: The store is created using configureStore with postsApi.reducer and postsApi.middleware.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Include both the reducer (under postsApi.reducerPath) and middleware from postsApi in the store configuration.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a store with configureStore and add postsApi.reducer and postsApi.middleware.

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'App' with a template section containing a div and a script section that exports the component.
steps.hint: Use export default with a template property and a div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named 'App' is created with a template containing a div and exported as default.
successCriteria: The component is named 'App', has a template with a div, and is exported as default.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Make sure the component has a template with a div and is exported as default.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a component with export default, a template that includes a div.

steps.title: Initialize the store in the Vue component
steps.instruction: In your Vue component's setup function, import the configured store and return it so it is available to the template.
steps.hint: Add a setup() function that returns an object containing the store.
steps.expectedOutcome: The store is returned from the setup function and available in the component.
successCriteria: The store is returned from the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Return the store from the setup function.

steps.title: Destructure the useGetPostsQuery hook
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, destructure the useGetPostsQuery hook from the postsApi.
steps.hint: The postsApi object exposes the generated hook. Use destructuring to extract it.

// Example: destructuring a hook from an API object
const { useGetDataQuery } = dataApi;

successCriteria: The useGetPostsQuery hook is destructured from postsApi in the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Call the useGetPostsQuery hook in setup

steps.hint: Call the hook (e.g. useGetPostsQuery()) to start fetching posts.
steps.analogousExample:
// Calling a hook in Vue setup

steps.expectedOutcome: The useGetPostsQuery hook is called in the setup function, triggering the data fetch.
successCriteria: The useGetPostsQuery hook is called in the setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Call useGetPostsQuery() inside the setup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Call the useGetPostsQuery hook inside the setup function to fetch the posts data.

steps.title: Destructure the query result
steps.instruction: Destructure data, isLoading, and error from the result object returned by useGetPostsQuery.
steps.hint: Use object destructuring on the hook result to extract data, isLoading, and error.
steps.analogousExample:
// Destructuring from query result
const { data, isLoading, error } = useGetPostsQuery();
steps.expectedOutcome: The query result is destructured into data, isLoading, and error for use in the template.
successCriteria: data, isLoading, and error are destructured from the query result and returned from setup.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Destructure data, isLoading, and error from the query result and include them in the return object.
steps.feedbackWrong: Destructure data, isLoading, and error from the useGetPostsQuery() result and return them from setup.

successCriteria: The template contains a list that iterates over the data and renders each post's title.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add a refetch button to demonstrate cache
steps.instruction: In the template, add a button with the text 'Refetch Posts' that calls the refetch function when clicked. Destructure refetch from the query result in setup and return it.
steps.hint: Add refetch to the destructuring from useGetPostsQuery(), return it from setup, and use @click="refetch" on the button.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button that triggers a refetch
<button @click="refetch">Refresh Data</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button triggers a data refetch when clicked, demonstrating RTK Query's cache behavior.
successCriteria: A button with 'Refetch Posts' is added and its click handler calls the refetch function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Add refetch to the destructured result, return it from setup, and add a button with @click that calls refetch.
